identity.title: Perfectoid signature, perfectoid Hilbert-Kunz multiplicity, and an application to local fundamental groups
identity.authors: Hanlin Cai; Seungsu Lee; Linquan Ma; Karl Schwede; Kevin Tucker

reviewed_version: arXiv:2209.04046v4, 88-page author manuscript; exact version visible in PDF and arXiv metadata; journal-version equivalence not established
summary: An impossible natural map from the completed cone to the specified p-adically completed graded absolute integral closure leaves the global geometric application without its stated proof. A separate exact normalized-length calculation corrects two auxiliary constants while preserving the qualitative conclusions. No counterexample to a theorem is claimed.

problems.title: The completed cone cannot map naturally to the specified target
problems.claim: Claim 7.0.5 uses a natural S -> S_1 -> T, where S is the homogeneous-maximal-ideal completion of S' and T is the p-adic completion of S'^{+,GR}, to apply Proposition 5.2.3 and prove the cone is BCM-regular.
assumptions: The section ring S' is finite graded over A''=W(k)[[y_1,...,y_s]][x_0,...,x_r].
C=S'^{+,GR} is integral over S' under its stated definition.
x_0 is in the homogeneous maximal ideal used to complete S'.
The asserted natural map is a unital S'-algebra map.

The geometric application retains normality, completeness, algebraically closed residue field, equidimensional fibers, log-Fano ampleness and global +-regularity for sufficiently small positive boundaries.

argument: 1-x_0 is a unit in S, with inverse the homogeneous-maximal-ideal-adically convergent geometric series.
The ideal (p,y_1,...,y_s,x_0-1,x_1,...,x_r) is a maximal ideal of A'' with quotient k.
By integrality and lying over, a prime q of C lies above it.
T=lim C/p^n C maps unitaly to C/pC and then the nonzero ring C/q, sending 1-x_0 to zero.
Therefore 1-x_0 is not a unit in T. No natural unital S'-algebra map S -> T exists.

problems.result: The specified factorization is impossible and the local-cohomology tensor product cannot use the asserted algebra structure. This is not a counterexample to the theorem conclusion.
counterevidence: The actual PDF p75 explicitly uses the two distinct completion topologies; TeX agrees.
Full-source GR-notation search found no prior localization or alternate complete-base definition.
Local cohomology can sometimes acquire a completed-base module structure; that does not supply the algebra structure explicitly required by Proposition 5.2.3.
An appropriate changed target may repair the proof, but its perfectoidness, maps and local-cohomology injection have not been verified.
problems.impact: Major at the claim level because the failed map is the necessary bridge to an explicitly advertised global geometric theorem. The local fundamental-group theorem, class-group bound and signature constructions are not shown to fail.

correction.requested_scope: Construct a suitable target receiving S_1 and prove compatible perfectoid structure, roots and preservation of the twisted top-local-cohomology injection, or supply a separate proof of the cone claim.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: A''=W(k)[[y]][x0,...,xr] embeds finitely/integrally into S'; C=S'^{+,GR} is integral over it. The proper maximal ideal (p,y...,x0?1,x1,...,xr) has residue k, hence lying over gives q in C with p,1?x0 in q. T=lim C/p^mC has a unital map to the nonzero C/q, so1?x0 is not a unit in T. In the homogeneous completion S, x0 lies in the maximal ideal, so1?x0 is a unit. Therefore no natural unital S'-algebra map S->T extending the given inclusion exists.
independent_acceptance.counterevidence: This is not a statement that every abstract ring map is impossible. A completed-base module action on local cohomology does not provide the required algebra structure from5.2.3. Localization or changed-target base completion may remove the unit obstruction, but would require separate perfectoidness, compatible roots, target map and survival of the graded-cover/local-cohomology injection.
independent_acceptance.impact: The invalid map is the bridge in Claim7.0.5 to the advertised global application7.0.4 and proof-based relaxation7.0.6. The conclusion is not refuted and no damage is established to all signature results, the separate local fundamental-group theorem or class-group bound.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: No full replacement target and injection proof verified. Retain this honest repair limitation; it is not an unproved confirmed theorem-falsity allegation.

problems.title: Total-degree simplex volume omitted in normalized-length constants
problems.claim: Lemma 4.0.13 uses length_A(A_n/I_n)>=p^(nd) epsilon^d; the final display of Theorem 5.4.11 assigns lambda(A_infinity/{v>=p^-e0})=p^-e0.
assumptions: A=W(k)[[x_2,...,x_d]], regular mixed characteristic with perfect residue field.
A_n adjoins p^n-th roots of all d regular parameters.
The stated valuation is total monomial degree, with v(p)=v(x_i)=1.
Normalized length scales finite-level A-length by p^(-nd).

check.kind: exact general combinatorial proof with independent finite diagnostic
check.input: q=p^n, a>0, I_a={c in A_infinity:v(c)>=a}, r_n=ceil(q a).

counterevidence: Both disputed expressions are present in the actual PDF, not extraction artifacts.
The printed scalars are correct in dimension one; floors/ceilings do not eliminate the dimension factor.
Main statements require qualitative positivity/vanishing, not those numerical values.
Theorem 5.4.10 supplies one positive threshold uniform over all socle injections.
problems.impact: Supported local error in auxiliary quantitative constants. The exact corrected positive bounds restore the lemma's contradiction and Theorem G's positive-infimum step. No central qualitative conclusion is shown damaged; Minor is based on that traced dependency, not on shortness of repair.

independent_acceptance.reasoning: With q=p^n, the regular local ring A_n has d parameters p^(1/q),x_i^(1/q), and v=q^-1*ord_mn. Thus I_a intersect A_n=m_n^ceil(qa), length_A=binom(ceil(qa)+d?1,d), and normalized limit a^d/d!. Residue fields coincide, so the lengths agree. The quotient is m_A-power torsion, and choosing integer N>=a makes p^N lie in I_a; completion modulo p^N does not alter this calculation.
independent_acceptance.decisive_checks: For d2,p2,n1,a1 the basis has three monomials instead of the printed lower bound4. For d2,p2,e0=1 the normalized length is1/8 rather than1/2. The error persists for arbitrarily large e0 in dimension>1 and cannot be fixed by a floor/ceiling convention. These are exact general/elementary checks, not a new execution of the historical48-case diagnostic.
independent_acceptance.repair_check: The corrected positive lower bound epsilon^d/d! gives the same zero-length contradiction. The rational-signature lower bound is p^(-d e0)/d!, with relative signature at least p^(-d e0)/(t*d!). Theorem5.4.10 supplies one epsilon uniform over socle injections: the descending nonzero tail spans stabilize in a t-dimensional space, and products of at most t annihilators with valuations tending to0 kill one fixed nonzero socle element, contradicting BCM-rationality via the stated BCM dependency.
independent_acceptance.severity_basis: The erroneous numerical constants are auxiliary to qualitative vanishing/positivity equivalences. The exact corrected constants and uniform-infimum argument restore the required implications with the same hypotheses, so no central qualitative damage is shown.

clarifications.text: The class-group bound is proved for some adapted choices of parameters. Parameter independence remains conjectural; no false arbitrary-parameter bound has been established by this review.

repair_verification: Problem1: no complete repair verified. Problem2: corrected local bounds and qualitative implications verified.
delivery_scope: Initial review complete for declared acquired-version scope; independent acceptance and author adoption not performed.

independent_acceptance.summary: Focused independent acceptance confirms the impossible natural completed-cone algebra map (Major) and the dimension-dependent normalized-length error (Minor). The exact corrected count and a genuinely uniform valuation threshold preserve the stated qualitative positivity implications. No theorem counterexample or whole-paper validation is asserted.
independent_acceptance.scope: Existing M25-0131-P1 and P2, including their assumptions, local/global dependency boundary, counterevidence, correction status and relevant parameter-choice clarification. Exact arXiv:2209.04046v4 dated3July2025,88pages; no publisher-version equivalence.
independent_acceptance.conclusion: Retain P1 Major with full target-algebra repair unverified; retain P2 Minor with exact local correction verified. Current scientific report is consistent with that limited result and needs no TeX/PDF change.
